downloadedSourceCountNote: Zero is correct. Three candidate binaries were retrieved into temporary storage outside the repository for provenance and measurement and were discarded. Nothing entered version control, no materialization destination was written and no receipt was created — this job owns no authority asset path and no receipt path. The provenance and hashes the assignment requires are recorded below as measurements, not as deposits.

method.description: Public official download from the Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles. The issuer's forms index is client-rendered and exposes no form links in server-rendered HTML, so the binaries were located by a domain-restricted search of the issuer's own host and then retrieved directly from paroles.alabama.gov. Three distinct binaries answer to the same form number and all three are live on the official host; each was retrieved, hashed, measured and read.
method.tooling: curl for retrieval and HTTP status; sha256 and byte counts on retrieved bytes; poppler (pdfinfo, pdftotext -layout) for structure and face text
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition requires using only the assigned public official sources, recording provenance and hashes, and stopping if identity, revision or issuer authority is uncertain. Identity and issuer authority are established and every hash is recorded. Revision is uncertain — three live binaries, only one dated — so the job records all three and stops short of naming one current.
method.onlyOfficialHostUsed: Every retrieved URL is on paroles.alabama.gov. A domain-restricted search was used to locate paths the client-rendered index does not expose; the search results were used as a path index only, and every byte came from the issuer.

finding.headline: ABPP-3 is not one binary. The Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles serves three distinct PDFs at three paths under that form number, all live at HTTP 200, and they are not three copies of one form: two are a three-page PARDON APPLICATION and the third is a four-page PARDON AND/OR REMISSION OF FINES APPLICATION. Only one of the three carries a printed revision, and it is the oldest.
finding.acquisitionRequiredRationale: Retrievability is proven three times over and every digest is pinned. What is not established is which of the three the Bureau treats as current, and no further retrieval answers that — it needs the issuer's own index, which is client-rendered.

resolvedIdentity.documentIdEvidence: Printed as the first line of page 1 on all three retrieved binaries. The form number is stable across every variant; it is the title, the page count and the scope that move.
resolvedIdentity.issuer: Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles
resolvedIdentity.issuerNote: The agency's own site styles it 'Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles' in its page titles and 'Alabama Board of Pardons and Paroles' in its organization metadata and logo caption. Both appear on the official host. The queue records the Board form. Recorded as observed; the Bureau/Board distinction is not adjudicated here.
resolvedIdentity.issuerAuthorityBasis: Ala. Admin. Code chapter 640-X-3 is published on the same official host as the Board's administrative code for pardons, and the site records that investigations for pardons, voter-rights restoration and remissions of fines and forfeitures are conducted by the Pardon Unit upon receipt of an application.
resolvedIdentity.scopeBasis: A single state agency with statewide jurisdiction over pardons. There is no county variant and no venue selector. Scope follows from the issuing body, not from the mailing address on the form.
resolvedIdentity.officialTitleRecorded: Alabama Board of Pardons and Paroles, forms
resolvedIdentity.officialTitleRecordedAssessment: Not a title. It is the name of the index page the identity was normalized from. The real titles are printed on the faces and differ between variants, which is precisely why this row could not be corrected by a single value.
resolvedIdentity.landingPageLimitation: The page returns HTTP 200 and 103,398 bytes of fully client-rendered content. Its server-rendered HTML contains no ABPP form links at all — the only ABPP-bearing URLs in the markup are social-media and payment-portal links. Which binary the Bureau currently publishes therefore cannot be read from the index.

retrievedBinaries.label: four-page pardon and remission variant
retrievedBinaries.printedTitle: PARDON AND/OR REMISSION OF FINES APPLICATION
retrievedBinaries.revisionFromUrlOnlyCaveat: A filename is a property of a file and a server, not a marking on the document. It is recorded as a path observation and is NOT promoted to a revision. The same rule was applied to the Idaho BCI application, whose REV-UNKNOWN was defended for exactly this reason.
retrievedBinaries.scopeOfTheForm: covers pardon and remission of fines in one instrument, with a printed selector reading 'FOR: PARDON☐  REMISSION OF FINES☐  BOTH☐'
distinguishingFaceText: Is the pardon based on claim of innocence?
Have you applied for a pardon or remission of fines before? Pardon ☐ Fines ☐ Neither ☐
retrievedBinaries.assessment: The strongest candidate for current on content grounds: it is the only one that is retitled to cover both remedies, the only four-page variant, and the only one whose path asserts a 2025 version. None of that is a printed revision.

retrievedBinaries.label: three-page pardon-only variant, dated
retrievedBinaries.printedRevisionLocation: on the face, the only printed revision marking found on any of the three
distinguishingFaceText: (Attach a complete list of convictions for which this pardon is requested.)
IS PARDON BASED ON CLAIM OF INNOCENCE: YES NO
retrievedBinaries.assessment: Demonstrably the oldest of the three by its own printed date, and superseded on content by the four-page variant. It is also the largest file, so byte size is no guide to currency.

retrievedBinaries.label: three-page pardon-only variant, undated
distinguishingFaceText: (Attach a complete list of charges for which this pardon is requested)
IS PARDON BASED ON CLAIM OF INNOCENCE: YES NO
retrievedBinaries.assessment: A third distinct document, not a copy of either other. Its item reads 'charges' where the October 2020 variant reads 'convictions' — a one-word difference with real legal weight, since a pardon operates on convictions. Which way that edit runs in time is not established.
retrievedBinaries.cleanestUrlIsNotTheNewest: This variant sits at the plainest, most guessable path — the one a reader would reach for first — and it is not the four-page current-content candidate. Path tidiness is not currency.

supersessionAssessment.establishedOnContent: The four-page PARDON AND/OR REMISSION OF FINES APPLICATION supersedes the pardon-only three-page form in scope: it absorbs remission of fines into the same instrument with an explicit three-way selector. That is a substantive expansion, not a reformat.
supersessionAssessment.establishedOnDate: Only one variant carries a printed date, Revised October 2020, and it is a pardon-only three-page form. It is therefore older than the retitled variant on content grounds regardless of what the other paths assert.
notEstablished: Which of the two three-page variants is older than the other. One is dated October 2020 and the other is undated, and an undated file may predate or postdate a dated one.
Whether the Bureau still accepts the pardon-only form, or whether it is retired.
Whether the four-page variant is the current publication or a parallel offering.
The direction of the 'charges' versus 'convictions' edit.
supersessionAssessment.adjacentFormObservation: The issuer separately publishes ABPP-5, Remission of Fine and/or Forfeiture Application, on the same host. If ABPP-3 has absorbed remission of fines, the relationship between the two is a question this record raises and does not answer. It is not assigned here and no inference is drawn.
supersessionAssessment.liveHttp200IsNotCurrency: All three superseded-or-not candidates return HTTP 200 on the issuer's own host. This is the same trap already recorded for the Florida Administrative Code, where nine superseded reference ids remain live. An official host serving a file says nothing about whether the issuer treats it as current.

commercialUseAndLicensing.whatWasObserved: The site footer reads '© 2026 Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles'. No terms-of-use page, licence or reuse statement was located, and none of the three retrieved binaries carries a copyright or reuse legend on its face.
commercialUseAndLicensing.assessment: A bare copyright footer is a weak assertion of rights, not a licence and not silence. It is materially different from the express reservation found on the Arizona courts site, which added 'Any rights not expressly granted herein are reserved', and different again from the genuine silence found on the Florida rules host.
commercialUseAndLicensing.doNotInfer: Public downloadability is not permission. generationAllowed must not be set true on the strength of this record.
commercialUseAndLicensing.queueRecordedPosition: The queue records the commercial-use terms as unresolved. That remains the correct value; this record supplies the observation behind it rather than changing it.
commercialUseAndLicensing.escalation: A definitive answer needs counsel or a written Bureau response. Human-only and outside this assignment.

doNotSubstitute.document: ABPP-5, Remission of Fine and/or Forfeiture Application
doNotSubstitute.why: A separate form on the same host covering remission alone. Now that ABPP-3's four-page variant also covers remission, the two overlap and are unusually easy to confuse. They are different form numbers.
Carries the only printed date of the three and is superseded on content by the retitled four-page variant. Same form number, different scope.

doNotSubstitute.document: the undated three-page PARDON APPLICATION at the plainest path
doNotSubstitute.why: The most guessable URL and not the current-content candidate. Its 'charges' wording differs from the October 2020 variant's 'convictions'.
The Board's administrative rules for pardons, published as a PDF on the same host. Authority, not an application form. Binding a rule as a participant filing would repeat the Illinois Rule 298 error.

doNotSubstitute.document: the Courtesy Notice Registration Form for Pardons
doNotSubstitute.why: A victim-notification registration form on the same host, not an applicant's pardon application.

doNotSubstitute.document: the ABPP Request to View Public Records form
doNotSubstitute.why: A records-request form on the same host with a June 2025 revision, close in date to the ABPP-3 four-page variant and easily mistaken for it in a search result list.
None was used. Every byte recorded here came from paroles.alabama.gov.

sourceContractEligibility.why: An exact source contract pins one digest. Three live binaries answer to this form number and the issuer's index does not disclose which is current, so there is no defensible single digest to pin. Pinning any of the three today would pin a guess.
sourceContractEligibility.whatWouldMakeItEligible: A reading of the Bureau's rendered forms index identifying the current ABPP-3, or a printed revision on the four-page variant.

edition13Impact.requiresNewBytesDetail: The adopted edition retains no Alabama pardon application. Bytes are freely retrievable at three pinned digests; which to admit is the open question.
edition13Impact.requiresTitleCorrectionDetail: The recorded officialTitle is an index page name. The correct title depends on which binary is admitted — 'Pardon and/or Remission of Fines Application' for the four-page variant, 'Pardon Application' for either three-page variant.
edition13Impact.requiresRevisionCorrectionDetail: The queue records the revision as unconfirmed. Only one candidate carries a printed revision, Revised October 2020, and it is not the current-content candidate. If the four-page variant is admitted, its revision must be recorded as unknown rather than taken from its filename.
edition13Impact.requiresLicenseDispositionNote: Unresolved. A bare copyright footer, no terms page located. generation_allowed must remain no.
edition13Impact.doNotAdmitAllThree: One form number, one row. Admitting more than one ABPP-3 row would manufacture documents the Bureau does not distinguish by number. The superseded variants belong in a supersession record, not in parallel rows.

sourceMaterializationEligibility.laterMaterializationPermittedDetail: All three are freely and publicly retrievable at HTTP 200 with no authentication, at digests pinned here. Once the current one is identified and the successor edition admits it, materialization is mechanical.
sourceMaterializationEligibility.notPermittedYetDetail: There is no canonical path to receipt against, no determination of which binary is current, and no licence position. Materializing a guess would pin the wrong digest for a participant-facing primary filing.

implementationFamilyEffect.effectOfThisJob: The Alabama pardon application moves from an unmanifested identity with a null issuer, an index-page title and no retrievability evidence to a confirmed statewide agency form with three pinned digests, three read faces, a content-based supersession direction and a precisely stated currency question. No implementation job depends on this identity, so nothing is released; what changes is that the acquisition question is now bounded rather than open-ended.
implementationFamilyEffect.familyReadinessStatement: The Alabama official-PDF family remains fail-closed and this job does not move it. The edition retains no Alabama pardon asset, currency is undetermined among three candidates, licensing is unresolved, generation is not permitted, runtime is disabled and no field map is built. No packet becomes generatable and no renderer is assigned.
implementationFamilyEffect.rendererObservation: All three candidates are unrotated Letter AcroForms. That is the acroform_fill shape. Field and widget counts were not enumerated because the binary that would be mapped is not yet identified, and mapping the wrong one would be wasted. An observation about the artifacts; no lane is assigned.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not unresolved_identity: the form number, issuer, role, scope and bound component are established and three binaries are pinned. It is not acquired_and_current: three live candidates differ in title, page count and scope, and the issuer's index does not disclose which is current. It is not blocked: the host answers every request at HTTP 200. The stop condition directs stopping where revision is uncertain, and it is uncertain in an unusually concrete way — not missing, but ambiguous between three.

expectedDownstreamEffect: The Alabama pardon application acquires provenance for the first time: three official URLs, three HTTP 200 confirmations, three digests, three byte counts, three read faces and a content-based supersession direction showing the four-page pardon-and-remission variant expanding on the pardon-only form. A recorded title that was really an index page name is identified as such. A concrete trap is named — three live binaries at one form number on the issuer's own host, with the plainest URL not the current-content candidate and the only printed date sitting on a superseded variant. The remaining work narrows from acquire-and-identify to one question: which of three the Bureau publishes today. No binary enters version control, no receipt is created, no component is rebound, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.

residualBlockers.reopenCondition: Closed by reading the rendered forms index, or by a printed revision appearing on the four-page variant.

residualBlockers.question: The current-content candidate carries no printed revision; only its filename asserts June 2025.

residualBlockers.question: The two three-page variants differ in whether the applicant attaches a list of 'charges' or of 'convictions', and the direction of that edit in time is unknown.
residualBlockers.why: A pardon operates on convictions, so the wording is not cosmetic.

residualBlockers.question: How ABPP-3's absorption of remission of fines relates to the separately published ABPP-5 Remission of Fine and/or Forfeiture Application.
Whether the Bureau permits redistribution of its forms.
